patches.value: For every tau>0 and positive integer J, consider the uniform grid t_j=j*tau, j=0,...,J, on [0,J*tau]. For every integer n with 0<=n<J, put a=t_n=n*tau. In particular n=0 is an admissible step for every tau>0, with a=t_0=0 and t_1=tau. For 0<sigma<=1, t in [a,a+tau], and constant mean-zero f,g in H^sigma, the source bilinear stage F_a(t;f,g) satisfies ||F_a(t;f,g)||_(H^beta)<=C*tau^((1+sigma-beta)/(1+sigma-beta0))*||f||_(H^sigma)*||g||_(H^sigma) for every beta in [beta0,1+sigma]. Here beta0=2*sigma-3/2 if 0<sigma<1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsilon for any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0 if sigma=1/2, and beta0=sigma-1 if 1/2<sigma<=1. Norms in this source assertion are unnormalized; C can depend on sigma and on a fixed epsilon, but not on tau, n, J or spectral support. The grid horizon J*tau is auxiliary and need not equal the problem parameter T.

value.context: Sections 1-2 and 3.3: 2*pi-periodic functions, coefficients normalized by 1/(2*pi) but function norms use unnormalized dx; P deletes zero mode. Interval endpoints nonnegative, length bounded by a fixed constant. Source estimates are uniform in time level, timestep and spectral support. The source convergence theorem is not imported. The grid is explicitly t_n=n*tau, n=0,...,L, tau=T/L (p.4; repeated p.20). Lemma 7.2 applies to every step 0<=n<L, including n=0. For an arbitrary positive tau, take the auxiliary source horizon J*tau with any positive integer J (in particular J=1); this gives an admissible source base zero without an extra premise. Equations (7.2)-(7.3) define its time-independent mean-zero bilinear stage; the proof on pp.33-34 derives bounds from integrals of length at most tau and endpoint norm bounds, without a solution or convergence hypothesis.

patches.value: For an arbitrary base a>=0, direct substitution s=a+r in Stage gives F_a(a+s;w,w)=S_(-a)F_0(s;S_a w,S_a w) for 0<=s<=tau. The Fourier multipliers S_a and S_(-a) preserve each Sobolev norm, reality and zero mean. For this positive tau, E003 supplies the auxiliary grid with J=1, t_0=0 and t_1=tau; n=0 satisfies 0<=n<J. Apply E003 at this admissible grid base t_0=0 to both inputs S_a w, at beta=a_sigma and beta=1+sigma. Since 0<tau<=1 and the exponent at a_sigma is >=sigma, tau^theta<=tau^sigma. The resulting normalized bounds are C_sigma*M^2*tau^sigma and C_sigma*M^2; fixed sqrt(2*pi) factors are absorbed in C_sigma. This proves both stage bounds at every a>=0, not only grid bases. Together with F001 and F002, discharge L1 and quantify the data.
